newsitem.title: UK: Blair pledges tough action if British MP charged.
newsitem.headline: Blair pledges tough action if British MP charged.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Wednesday he would take firm disciplinary action against one of his Labour MPs if inquiries into allegations of bribery turn up any "improprieties".

Mohammed Sarwar, elected in the May 1 general election as Britain's first Moslem MP, is suing a newspaper which made the allegations. But he has admitted giving a 5,000 pound ($8,270) loan to one of his rival candidates in the Glasgow Govan constituency.

Blair, determined not to allow his government to be weighed down by the sort of sleaze scandals which hit John Major's previous Conservative administration, told Labour's National Executive the party had set itself very high standards.
"We did that deliberately, very deliberately, and we must meet them," an aide quoted Blair as telling the meeting.
Police are already looking into the allegations against Sarwar and the Executive set up a three-person committee to conduct its own investigation.
"Whether or not there are police charges and convictions, if there is any impropriety found by us, there will be disciplinary action," the Blair aide said.
If such impropriety was serious, Sarwar might be banned from standing for Labour in future elections, he said.
He added: "If police charges are made, the whip will be removed pending the outcome of those charges."
The removal of the whip is a technical move. It would Sarwar ceasing to be a member of the parliamentary Labour Party, while remaining an MP.
The claims against Sarwar are the first dark cloud to gather over the new government, which was helped to its landslide victory by allegations of sleaze against Conservative politicians.
Throughout the election campaign, Blair contrasted his firm approach to party discipline with what he described as the weak and dithering approach of defeated prime minister Major.

Sarwar, 46, moved to Scotland from Pakistan at the age of four. He became a millionaire after building up a successful grocery business and has been involved in the Labour Party for more than 10 years.
But his selection was a bitter struggle with a former MP, Mike Watson, whose constituency was abolished by a commission redrawing electoral boundaries.

The selection battle gave rise to allegations of irregularities in the registration of Labour party members. Police are also investigating the eligibility of almost 300 people who were included late on the electoral roll.
In the election, Sarwar won with 2,914 more votes than his nearest rival, the Scottish National Party's Nicola Sturgeon.
